questions.q: What does the Data pane show in the Tableau Desktop workspace?
options: Every field from your connected data source, split into Dimensions and Measures
A list of every worksheet in the current workbook
The SQL query Tableau is about to run
Only the fields currently placed on a shelf
questions.explain: The Data pane lists every available field from the connection, already split into Dimensions and Measures.

questions.q: What determines the basic structure of a Tableau view — what's on the horizontal vs. vertical axis?
options: What fields are placed on the Columns and Rows shelves
The order fields appear in the Data pane
The Analytics pane
The Format menu
questions.explain: Columns and Rows are the shelves that set up a view's basic horizontal/vertical structure — everything else layers on top of that.

questions.q: In the labeled 'Parts of the View' screenshot, what creates the row headers (label A)?
options: A discrete field's distinct values, such as Category
A continuous field creating a numeric axis
The Marks card's color encoding
The worksheet's caption
questions.explain: Row and column headers come from discrete fields — each distinct value in the field becomes its own header/label.

questions.q: What is a 'caption' in a Tableau worksheet view?
options: A short auto-generated or custom description of what the view shows
The name of the workbook file
A tooltip that appears only on hover
The axis scale for a continuous measure
questions.explain: The caption is the small text block, usually at the bottom of a view, that summarizes what the chart is showing.

questions.q: Where do you find the tabs for switching between different worksheets, dashboards, and stories in the same workbook?
options: Along the bottom of the workbook window, similar to sheet tabs in Excel
In the Data pane, under a 'Sheets' folder
In the Analysis menu only
There are no tabs — each worksheet is a separate file
questions.explain: Every worksheet, dashboard, and story in a Tableau workbook gets its own tab at the bottom of the window, just like Excel sheet tabs.
